title.raw: 卷四十二 志第三十二 地理六 Volume 42 Treatises 36: Gepgraphy 6

sentences.zh: 劍南道劍南道，蓋古梁州之域，漢蜀郡、廣漢、犍為、越巂、益州、牂柯、巴郡之地，總為鶉首分。

translations.literal: The Jiannan Circuit, Jiannan Circuit — broadly the territory of ancient Liang Province, the lands of the Han commanderies of Shu, Guanghan, Jianwei, Yuexi, Yizhou, Zangge, and Ba, all grouped under the Quail's Head allotment.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiannan Circuit comprised broadly the domain of ancient Liang Province — the Han-era territories of Shu, Guanghan, Jianwei, Yuexi, Yizhou, Zangge, and Ba commanderies — all assigned to the Quail's Head stellar allotment.

sentences.zh: 為府一，都護府一，州三十八，縣百八十九。

translations.literal: It had one superior prefecture, one Protectorate General, thirty-eight prefectures, and one hundred eighty-nine counties.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit contained one superior prefecture, one Protectorate General, thirty-eight prefectures, and one hundred eighty-nine counties.

translations.literal: Its famous mountains: Min, E, Qingcheng, and Heming.
translations.idiomatic: Notable mountains included Min, Emei, Qingcheng, and Heming.

translations.literal: Its great rivers: the Jiang, Fu, Luo, and Xihan.
translations.idiomatic: Its major rivers were the Yangzi, Fu, Luo, and Xihan.

translations.literal: Its levies: silk, cotton, ramie, and zhufiber.
translations.idiomatic: Standard levies included silk, cotton, ramie, and zhufiber cloth.

sentences.zh: 厥貢：金、布、絲、葛、羅、綾、綿紬、羚角、犛尾。

translations.literal: Its tribute: gold, cloth, silk, ramie, gauze, damask, cotton pongee, antelope horns, and yak tails.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute items included gold, cloth, silk, ramie, gauze, damask, cotton pongee, antelope horns, and yak tails.

translations.literal: Chengdu Superior Prefecture, Chengdu Superior Prefecture, Shu Commandery, red grade.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu Superior Prefecture (Shu Commandery), red grade.

sentences.zh: 至德二載曰南京，為府，上元元年罷京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide it was called the Southern Capital and made a superior prefecture; in the first year of Shangyuan its status as a capital was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 757 it was designated the Southern Capital and elevated to a superior prefecture; in 758 its capital status was revoked.

sentences.zh: 土貢：錦、單絲羅、高杼布、麻、蔗糖、梅煎、生春酒。

translations.literal: Local tribute: brocade, single-thread gauze, high-loom cloth, hemp, cane sugar, plum syrup, and raw spring wine.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute comprised brocade, single-thread gauze, high-loom cloth, hemp, cane sugar, plum syrup, and raw spring wine.

sentences.zh: 戶十六萬九百五十，口九十二萬八千一百九十九。

translations.idiomatic: It registered 160,950 households and a population of 928,199.
It administered ten counties.

sentences.zh: 有府三，曰威遠、歸德、二江。

translations.literal: It had three garrison prefectures, called Weiyuan, Guide, and Erjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Three garrison prefectures were attached: Weiyuan, Guide, and Erjiang.

sentences.zh: 有天征軍，本天威，乾元二年置，元和三年更名。

translations.literal: There was the Tianzheng Army, originally Tianwei, established in the second year of Qianyuan and renamed in the third year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianzheng Army was stationed here; originally called Tianwei, it was established in 759 and renamed in 808.
Chengdu County, second-rank red grade.

translations.literal: It had a shrine to the River Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine to the River Spirit stood within the county.

sentences.zh: 北十八里有萬歲池，天寶中，長史章仇兼瓊築隄，積水溉田。

translations.literal: Eighteen li north was Wansui Pool; in the Tianbao era the prefectural secretary Zhang Qiu Jianqiong built a dike, impounding water to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen li to the north lay Wansui Pool; during the Tianbao period the prefectural secretary Zhang Qiu Jianqiong built a dike there to store water for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 南百步有官源渠隄百餘里，天寶二載，令獨孤戒盈築。

translations.literal: A hundred paces south was the Guanyuan Canal dike, over a hundred li long, built in the second year of Tianbao by Magistrate Dugu Jieying.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred paces south stood the Guanyuan Canal dike, more than a hundred li in length, constructed in 743 by Magistrate Dugu Jieying.
Huayang County, second-rank red grade.

sentences.zh: 本蜀，貞觀十七年析成都置，乾元元年更名。

translations.literal: Originally Shu; in the seventeenth year of Zhenguan it was split off from Chengdu and established, and in the first year of Qianyuan it was renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly called Shu, it was carved out of Chengdu and established in 643, receiving its present name in 758.
Xindu County, second-rank capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: Established in the second year of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: It was established in 619.
Mount Fanyang lay within the county.
Xipu County, second-rank capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong it was split off from Chengdu and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Chengdu and established in 686.
Xinfan County, second-rank capital-vicinity grade.
Shuangliu County, second-rank capital-vicinity grade.
Guangdu County, second-rank capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo it was split off from Shuangliu and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Shuangliu and established in 662.
Pi County, second-rank capital-vicinity grade.
Wenjiang County, second-rank capital-vicinity grade.

sentences.zh: 本萬春，武德三年置，貞觀元年更名。

translations.literal: Originally Wanchun; established in the third year of Wude and renamed in the first year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wanchun, it was established in 620 and received its present name in 627.

sentences.zh: 有新源水，開元二十三年，長史章仇兼瓊因蜀王秀故渠開，通漕西山竹木。

translations.literal: There was the Xinyuan River; in the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan the prefectural secretary Zhang Qiu Jianqiong opened the old canal of Prince Xiu of Shu, enabling transport by water of bamboo and timber from the western hills.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinyuan River flowed here; in 735 the prefectural secretary Zhang Qiu Jianqiong reopened the old canal of Prince Xiu of Shu to float bamboo and timber from the western hills by water.
Lingchi County.
Second-rank capital-vicinity grade.

sentences.zh: 本東陽，久視元年置，天寶元年更名。

translations.literal: Originally Dongyang; established in the first year of Jiushi and renamed in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Dongyang, it was established in 700 and received its present name in 742.

translations.literal: Peng Prefecture, Peng Prefecture, Mengyang Commandery, dense grade.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Prefecture (Mengyang Commandery), dense grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong it was split off from Yizhou and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Yizhou and established in 686.

translations.literal: Local tribute: segment-pattern gauze and crossed-weft silk.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included segment-pattern gauze and crossed-weft silk.

sentences.zh: 戶五萬五千九百二十二，口三十五萬七千三百八十七。

translations.idiomatic: It registered 55,922 households and a population of 357,387.
It administered four counties.

translations.literal: It had two garrison prefectures, called Tianshui and Tangxing.
translations.idiomatic: Two garrison prefectures were attached: Tianshui and Tangxing.
The Weirong Army was stationed here.

sentences.zh: 有羊灌田、朋笮、繩橋三守捉城。

translations.literal: There were three garrison-collector posts: Yangguantian, Pengzha, and Shengqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Three garrison-collector posts stood at Yangguantian, Pengzha, and Shengqiao.

translations.literal: There were three fortified posts: Qipan, Anyuan, and Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Three fortified posts were maintained at Qipan, Anyuan, and Longxi.
The Dangfeng garrison was posted here.
Jingsai Pass guarded the frontier here.
Jiulong County, prominent grade.

sentences.zh: 武德三年以九隴、綿竹、導江置濛州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude Meng Prefecture was established from Jiulong, Mianzhu, and Daojiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 620 Meng Prefecture was created from Jiulong, Mianzhu, and Daojiang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年州廢，縣皆來屬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished and all counties came under this jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture was abolished in 628, its counties were all reassigned here.

sentences.zh: 武后時，長史劉易從決唐昌沲江，鑿川派流，合堋口埌歧水溉九隴、唐昌田，民為立祠。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time the prefectural secretary Liu Yicong cut through the Min River at Tangchang, opened channels to divide the flow, and joined the Pengkou levee with the Qishui to irrigate the fields of Jiulong and Tangchang; the people erected a shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign the prefectural secretary Liu Yicong breached the Min at Tangchang, cut diversion channels, and linked the Pengkou levee with the Qishui to irrigate fields in Jiulong and Tangchang; the people raised a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 有葛璝山、漓沅山、陽平山。

translations.literal: It had Mount Geji, Mount Liyuan, and Mount Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Geji, Mount Liyuan, and Mount Yangping lay within the county.
Daojiang County, prominent grade.

sentences.zh: 本盤龍，武德元年以故汶山置，尋更名。

translations.literal: Originally Panlong; in the first year of Wude it was established from former Wenshan and soon renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Panlong, it was established from the old Wenshan district in 618 and soon received its present name.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中曰灌寧，開元中復為導江。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era it was called Guanning; in the Kaiyuan era it reverted to Daojiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan period it was called Guanning; in the Kaiyuan period it was restored to Daojiang.

sentences.zh: 有侍郎堰，其東百丈堰，引江水以溉彭、益田，龍朔中築。

translations.literal: There was the Shilang Weir, and east of it the Baizhang Weir, drawing river water to irrigate the fields of Peng and Yi, built in the Longshuo era.
translations.idiomatic: The Shilang Weir stood here, and to its east the Baizhang Weir, which diverted river water to irrigate fields in Peng and Yi prefectures; both were built in the Longshuo period.

translations.literal: There was also a small weir, built at the beginning of the Chang'an era.
translations.idiomatic: A smaller weir was also constructed early in the Chang'an period.

translations.literal: To the west was Canya Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Canya Pass lay to the west;

translations.literal: there were Mount Min and Mount Yulei.
translations.idiomatic: and Mount Min and Mount Yulei stood within the county.

translations.literal: There was the Zhenjing Army, established in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenjing Army was posted here, established during the Kaiyuan period.

translations.literal: There was the Baisha garrison-collector post.
translations.idiomatic: The Baisha garrison-collector post was maintained here.

translations.literal: There were the Mugua and Sanqi garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Mugua and Sanqi garrisons were posted here.
Tangchang County, prominent grade.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年析九隴、導江、郫置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng it was split off from Jiulong, Daojiang, and Pi and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Jiulong, Daojiang, and Pi and established in 677.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年曰周昌，神龍元年復故名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou it was called Zhouchang; in the first year of Shendragon it reverted to the former name.
translations.idiomatic: In 693 it was renamed Zhouchang; in 705 it was restored to Tangchang.
Mengyang County.
Dense grade.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年析九隴、什邡、雒置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng it was split off from Jiulong, Shifang, and Luo and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Jiulong, Shifang, and Luo and established in 677.

translations.literal: Shu Prefecture, Shu Prefecture, Tang'an Commandery, dense grade.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Prefecture (Tang'an Commandery), dense grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong it was split off from Yizhou and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Yizhou and established in 686.

sentences.zh: 土貢：錦、單絲羅、花紗、紅藍、馬策。

translations.literal: Local tribute: brocade, single-thread gauze, patterned gauze, red indigo, and horse whips.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included brocade, single-thread gauze, patterned gauze, red indigo, and horse whips.

sentences.zh: 戶五萬六千五百七十七，口三十九萬六百九十四。

translations.idiomatic: It registered 56,577 households and a population of 390,694.
It administered four counties.

sentences.zh: 有府三，曰金堰、廣逢、灌口。

translations.literal: It had three garrison prefectures, called Jinyan, Guangfeng, and Guankou.
translations.idiomatic: Three garrison prefectures were attached: Jinyan, Guangfeng, and Guankou.

sentences.zh: 有鎮靜軍，乾符二年，節度使高駢置。

translations.literal: There was the Zhenjing Army, established in the second year of Qianfu by the military commissioner Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenjing Army was posted here, established in 875 by the military commissioner Gao Pian.
Jinyuan County, prominent grade.
Mount Tiancang lay within the county.
Qingcheng County, prominent grade.

translations.literal: The character "qing" (green) was formerly written "qing" (clear); it was changed in the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The name was formerly written with the character for "clear" rather than "green"; it was changed in 730.
Mount Qingcheng lay within the county.
Tang'an County, prominent grade.

translations.literal: Originally Tanglong; established in the first year of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tanglong, it was established in 618.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年曰武隆，神龍元年復為唐隆，先天元年更名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou it was called Wulong; in the first year of Shendragon it reverted to Tanglong; in the first year of Xiantian it was renamed.
translations.idiomatic: In 693 it was renamed Wulong; in 705 it was restored to Tanglong; in 712 it received its present name.
Xinjin County.
Prominent grade.

translations.literal: Two li southwest was the Yuanji Weir.
translations.idiomatic: Two li to the southwest stood the Yuanji Weir.

sentences.zh: 分四筒穿渠，溉眉州通義、彭山之田。

translations.literal: It divided into four sluice channels to irrigate the fields of Tongyi in Meizhou and Pengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Four sluice channels were cut from it to irrigate fields in Tongyi of Meizhou and in Pengshan.

sentences.zh: 開元二十八年，採訪使章仇兼瓊開。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Kaiyuan the investigation commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong opened it.
translations.idiomatic: It was opened in 740 by the investigation commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong.

sentences.zh: 有稠稉山、本竹山、天社山、主簿山。

translations.literal: It had Mount Choujing, Mount Benzhu, Mount Tianshe, and Mount Zhubu.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Choujing, Mount Benzhu, Mount Tianshe, and Mount Zhubu lay within the county.
Iron was mined here.

translations.literal: Han Prefecture, Han Prefecture, Deyang Commandery, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Han Prefecture (Deyang Commandery), upper grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong it was split off from Yizhou and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Yizhou and established in 686.

sentences.zh: 土貢：交梭，雙紃，彌牟、紵布，衫段，綾，紅藍，蜀馬。

translations.literal: Local tribute: crossed-weft silk, double-cord silk, Mimu and zhufiber cloth, jacket-segment silk, damask, red indigo, and Shu horses.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included crossed-weft silk, double-cord silk, Mimu and zhufiber cloth, jacket-segment silk, damask, red indigo, and Shu horses.

sentences.zh: 戶六萬九千五，口三十萬八千二百三。

translations.idiomatic: It registered 69,005 households and a population of 308,203.
It administered five counties.

translations.literal: It had one garrison prefecture, called Yujin.
translations.idiomatic: One garrison prefecture was attached: Yujin.
The Weisheng Army was stationed here.
Luo County, prominent grade.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，刺史盧士珵立隄堰，溉田四百餘頃。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era Prefect Lu Shirui built dikes and weirs, irrigating more than four hundred qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenyuan period Prefect Lu Shirui built dikes and weirs that irrigated more than four hundred qing of farmland.
Deyang County, dense grade.

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude it was split off from Luo and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Luo and established in 620.
Lutou Pass was here.
Shifang County, prominent grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude it was split off from Luo and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Luo and established in 619.
Mount Libingci lay within the county.
Mianzhu County, dense grade.

sentences.zh: 有庚除山、萬安山、鹿堂山。

translations.literal: It had Mount Gengchu, Mount Wan'an, and Mount Lutang.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Gengchu, Mount Wan'an, and Mount Lutang lay within the county.
Jintang County.
Upper grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng it was split off from Luo and Xindu and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Luo and Xindu and established in 671.
Mount Changli lay within the county.

translations.literal: Jia Prefecture, Jia Prefecture, Jianwei Commandery, middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Prefecture (Jianwei Commandery), middle grade.

sentences.zh: 本眉山郡，天寶元年更名。

translations.literal: Originally Meishan Commandery; renamed in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Meishan Commandery, it was renamed in 742.

translations.literal: Local tribute: bran-gold, purple kudzu, and musk.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included bran-gold, purple kudzu, and musk.

sentences.zh: 戶三萬四千二百八十九，口九萬九千五百九十一。

translations.idiomatic: It registered 34,289 households and a population of 99,591.
It administered eight counties.

sentences.zh: 有犍為、沐源、寺莊、牛徑、銅山、曲灘、陁和、平戎、依名、利雲、溶川、羅護、柘林、大池、雞心、龍溪、賴泥、可陽、婆籠、馬鞍、始犂、峨眉等二十二鎮兵。

translations.literal: There were twenty-two garrison-collector posts with troops: Jianwei, Muyuan, Sizhuang, Niujing, Tongshan, Qutan, Tuohe, Pingrong, Yiming, Liyun, Rongchuan, Luohu, Zhelin, Dachi, Jixin, Longxi, Laini, Keyang, Polong, Ma'an, Shili, and Emei.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two garrison-collector posts with troops were maintained here: Jianwei, Muyuan, Sizhuang, Niujing, Tongshan, Qutan, Tuohe, Pingrong, Yiming, Liyun, Rongchuan, Luohu, Zhelin, Dachi, Jixin, Longxi, Laini, Keyang, Polong, Ma'an, Shili, and Emei.
Longyou County, dense grade.
Pingqiang County, lower-middle grade.
Iron was produced here.
A pass was maintained here.
Emei County, upper grade.

translations.literal: It had gold; it had iron.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and iron were produced here.
Jiajiang County, upper grade.
Iron was produced here.
Yujin County, middle grade.
Suishan County, middle grade.

sentences.zh: 久視元年析置樂都縣，尋省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiushi Ledu County was split off and established, but soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Ledu County was carved out and established in 700 but was soon abolished.
Mount Sui lay within the county.
Luomu County, middle grade.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年開生獠置，以縣置沐州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde it was established by opening up the Sheng Liao; with the county Mu Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: It was established in 665 by opening territory of the Sheng Liao, and Mu Prefecture was created with the county as its seat.

sentences.zh: 高宗上元三年州廢，縣亦省，儀鳳三年復置，來屬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan of Emperor Gaozong the prefecture was abolished and the county also removed; in the third year of Yifeng it was restored and came under this jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In 676 the prefecture was abolished and the county removed; in 678 the county was restored and reassigned here.
Mount Emei lay within the county.
Jianwei County.
Middle grade.

sentences.zh: 本隸戎州，高宗上元元年來屬。

translations.literal: Originally subordinate to Rong Prefecture; in the first year of Shangyuan of Emperor Gaozong it came under this jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly subordinate to Rong Prefecture, it was reassigned here in 674.

translations.literal: Mei Prefecture, Mei Prefecture, Tongyi Commandery, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Prefecture (Tongyi Commandery), upper grade.

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude it was split off from Jia Prefecture and established.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved out of Jia Prefecture and established in 619.

translations.literal: Local tribute: bran-gold, citrus, rock honey, and kudzu powder.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included bran-gold, citrus, rock honey, and kudzu powder.

sentences.zh: 戶四萬三千五百二十九，口十七萬五千二百五十六。

translations.idiomatic: It registered 43,529 households and a population of 175,256.
It administered five counties.
Tongyi County, dense grade.
Pengshan County, dense grade.

translations.literal: Originally Longshan; subordinate to Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Longshan, it was subordinate to Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年省入通義，二年復置，來屬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan it was abolished and merged into Tongyi; in the second year it was restored and came under this jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: It was merged into Tongyi in 627, restored in 628, and reassigned here.

translations.literal: Renamed in the first year of Xiantian.
translations.idiomatic: It was renamed in 712.

sentences.zh: 有通濟大堰一，小堰十，自新津邛江口引渠南下，百二十里至州西南入江，溉田千六百頃，開元中，益州長史章仇兼瓊開。

translations.literal: There was one Tongji Great Weir and ten small weirs, drawing channels south from the Qionjiang mouth at Xinjin, one hundred twenty li to the southwest of the prefecture where they entered the river, irrigating one thousand six hundred qing of fields; opened in the Kaiyuan era by the Yizhou prefectural secretary Zhang Qiu Jianqiong.
translations.idiomatic: One Tongji Great Weir and ten smaller weirs diverted water south from the Qionjiang mouth at Xinjin, ran one hundred twenty li to enter the river southwest of the prefectural seat, and irrigated one thousand six hundred qing of fields; they were opened during the Kaiyuan period by the Yizhou prefectural secretary Zhang Qiu Jianqiong.
Salt was produced here.
Mount Pengnu lay within the county.
Danling County, upper grade.
Mount Longhu lay within the county.
Hongya County, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 武德元年以縣置犍州，五年省南安入焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude the county was made into Qian Prefecture; in the fifth year Nan'an was abolished and merged into it.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 the county became the seat of Qian Prefecture; in 622 Nan'an was merged into it.

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished and it came under this jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture was abolished in 627, it was reassigned here.

Pujiang County, lower-middle grade.

translations.idiomatic: From Qingxi Pass south through Dading Fort, one hundred ten li to Dashicheng; southwest through Jingkou one hundred twenty li to Yong'an Fort, which guarded the strategic junction of Dian and Zha.

translations.idiomatic: North of Yangpeng Ridge lay Xi Prefecture; to its south lay Nanzhao.

translations.idiomatic: In 652 the prefecture was abolished and the three counties were merged into Changming.
